entries.prompt: Perform ONLY a framing/padding correction on this ONE isolated Viper mask. Preserve the existing mask exactly: same nearly frontal camera, silhouette, broad split crown, thin center spine, muted red-brown paint motifs on black, amber eyes, three small viewer-right red temple dots, silver nasal relief, small dark breathing recesses, lower tube and all original visible details. Do not re-sculpt, symmetrize, recolor or repaint it. Reduce the complete mask uniformly to88% of its current size and recenter on an otherwise unchanged transparent canvas, keeping the source canvas aspect ratio. The complete mask should occupy about78% of canvas HEIGHT with roughly11% true clear transparent space above the top and below the lowest mouthpiece. Keep every edge/tip complete. No flesh, organic mandibles, dreads, body, shoulder cannon, orange environment lighting, new glyphs, extra vents/teeth/horns or glow. True transparent background, no floor/shadow, text, border or vignette. Return exactly one complete isolated native PNG, not multiple views.
entries.sourceGenerationPrompt: Create exactly ONE isolated removable biomask faithful to the photographed NECA Predator Series12 VIPER2014 toy sculpture and paint. This is VERSION A: source-faithful isolated reconstruction of this licensed toy edition, not an original movie mask, not a new PHG class, not Lost Tribe Scout. FIRST ATTACHMENT viper-catalog.jpg is the controlling color/camera/sculpt reference: use ONLY the MASKED HEAD in the UPPER-RIGHT INSET on white background. The MAIN BODY on that catalog is UNMASKED and must not supply mask geometry. The two other full-figure scene photographs help verify mask outlines/attachments only; their dramatic orange lighting is NOT paint and must not be introduced into the asset palette. Retain the same nearly frontal view and very slight downward-facing tilt shown in the catalog masked inset. Precisely copy its dark charcoal/black metallic face shell, broad twin rounded forehead lobes with the painted muted red/brown-red curving motifs surrounding the BLACK inner oval areas, the narrow tall central split/spine, angular brow and cheek planes, small amber eye lenses, small bright silver raised mechanical relief over the nasal bridge, two small adjacent dark breathing recesses and the existing small tubular silver-gray lower breathing mouthpiece. Preserve the small original temple targeting-dot cluster on the viewer-right where visible, without extending it into the nearby shoulder cannon or dreadlocks. The crown paint is subdued red-brown over black, NOT orange emissive paint, and the eyes are tiny amber lenses, NOT a new intense orange glow. Keep source-visible sculpt details modest and exact to the references; resolution is limited so do not add extra grilles, fangs, tusks, horns, glyphs, studs, new LED arrays or invented lower mouth machinery. Source-like photographed neutral toy-metal material and paint wear, not a stylized redesign or polished chrome. Remove wearer entirely: NO flesh, organic teeth/mandibles, dreads/hair, neck, collar/mesh, shoulder armor or cannon, body, fabric, weapons or background. The asset is only the removable continuous mask shell and proven attached mask fittings. Use a square transparent canvas with VERY GENEROUS negative-space padding: the entire mask occupies approximately960pixels on a1280pixel canvas, no more than78% of its longer canvas dimension, centered; at least10 to12% clear transparent margin around the outermost top and bottom. Do not enlarge to fill canvas. Preserve all mask tips with no clipping. Exactly one complete isolated mask, true alpha background, no plate/sheet, no inset, no extra view, no text, watermark, logo, border, floor shadow or vignette.
